learningObjectives: Integrate cellular, circuit, cognitive and contextual levels.
Distinguish causal mechanisms from correlates and markers.
Identify reductionist errors in clinical reasoning.

anatomy.label: Cellular level
anatomy.clinical: Medical and pharmacological factors may enter here.

anatomy.label: Circuit level
anatomy.clinical: Similar symptoms can arise from different circuit disruptions.

anatomy.label: Cognitive level
anatomy.detail: Mental operations bridge neural systems and behaviour.
anatomy.clinical: Assessment should specify the affected operation.

anatomy.label: Contextual level
anatomy.detail: Demand and support alter system expression.
anatomy.clinical: A capacity problem may appear only under certain conditions.

interaction.title: Explore Integrated Systems Capstone
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence.

stages.label: Describe
stages.text: Define the behaviour, time course and context precisely.

stages.label: Map
stages.text: Identify plausible operations and systems at multiple levels.

stages.label: Compare
stages.text: Test competing explanations and disconfirming evidence.

stages.label: Intervene
stages.text: Choose the safest, most modifiable leverage points.

stages.label: Update
stages.text: Revise the model using outcome and new information.

quizBank.question: A multilevel formulation should:
options: Link biological, cognitive, behavioural and contextual processes
quizBank.explanation: Clinical phenomena usually require linked levels of explanation.

quizBank.question: A neural correlate is:
options: An associated measure, not automatically a cause
quizBank.explanation: Association alone does not establish causal or clinical meaning.

quizBank.question: The strongest model is the one that:
options: Explains the pattern and guides testable action
quizBank.explanation: Clinical models should be useful, falsifiable and revisable.

quizBank.question: Reductionism risks:
options: Collapsing complex presentations into one level
quizBank.explanation: Single-level accounts often miss interacting causes and constraints.

quizBank.question: Neuroscience should be used to:
options: Refine assessment and intervention while preserving context
quizBank.explanation: Neuroscience is one evidence layer within broader clinical reasoning.

reviewPrompts: The best formulation is not the most biological one; it is the model that explains the pattern, survives alternatives and guides safe action.
